title: Propulsion
description: This syllabus is designed for a senior undergraduate aerospace propulsion course. It balances air-breathing engines, rockets, and emerging propulsion concepts while keeping performance analysis, thermodynamics, combustion, testing, and vehicle integration visible throughout.

topics.title: Propulsion Fundamentals and Thrust
topics.description: Builds the basic momentum, energy, and performance language used for propellers, jets, rockets, and advanced propulsion systems.

children.title: Momentum theory of thrust
children.description: Students learn how accelerating mass flow creates thrust and why propulsion is fundamentally a control-volume problem.

children.title: Propulsive performance metrics
children.description: Performance metrics let students compare engines across mission roles and operating conditions.

children.title: Flight condition effects
children.description: Propulsion performance changes with altitude, Mach number, inlet state, and vehicle speed.

topics.title: Thermodynamic Cycles for Engines
topics.description: Connects propulsion hardware to Brayton-cycle thermodynamics, energy addition, compression, expansion, and efficiency limits.

children.title: Brayton cycle analysis
children.description: The ideal gas-turbine cycle gives students a reference model for jet engines and gas turbines.

children.title: Real-cycle losses
children.description: Students learn how component inefficiencies, pressure losses, and temperature limits move performance away from ideal predictions.

children.title: Cycle performance trends
children.description: Cycle parameters are used to reason about fuel burn, thrust, bypass ratio, and engine architecture.

topics.title: Propellers and Propeller-Driven Systems
topics.description: Explains how rotating blades convert shaft power into thrust and why propellers are efficient for low-speed aircraft and emerging electric propulsion systems.

children.title: Actuator disk theory
children.description: Momentum theory gives a first-order estimate of induced velocity, thrust, and ideal propulsive efficiency.

children.title: Blade element concepts
children.description: Blade-element reasoning connects airfoil lift/drag to thrust and torque along the blade span.

children.title: Propeller integration
children.description: Students learn how propellers interact with engines, electric motors, airframes, and operating envelopes.

topics.title: Turbojet and Turbofan Engines
topics.description: Covers the major air-breathing engine families used in aircraft and explains how architecture choices shape thrust, fuel burn, and mission fit.

children.title: Turbojet operation
children.description: Turbojets show the simplest gas-turbine propulsion architecture and are useful for high-speed performance intuition.

children.title: Turbofan operation
children.description: Turbofans improve efficiency by accelerating a larger mass of air at a lower jet velocity.

children.title: Engine matching and mission fit
children.description: Students compare turbojets, low-bypass turbofans, and high-bypass turbofans across flight regimes.

topics.title: Inlets, Compressors, and Turbines
topics.description: Focuses on the turbomachinery and inlet components that condition flow, raise pressure, extract work, and determine operability.

children.title: Inlet/diffuser performance
children.description: Inlets slow and condition incoming air with minimum total-pressure loss and distortion.

children.title: Compressor fundamentals
children.description: Compressors raise pressure but must avoid stall, surge, and efficiency loss.

children.title: Turbine fundamentals
children.description: Turbines extract work from hot gas to drive the compressor and fan while surviving severe thermal loading.

topics.title: Combustors, Fuels, Emissions, and Nozzles
topics.description: Links chemical energy release to thrust production while addressing stability, emissions, temperature limits, and exhaust expansion.

children.title: Combustion fundamentals
children.description: Students learn what makes a flame stable, efficient, and compatible with high-speed air flow.

children.title: Aviation fuels and emissions
children.description: Fuel choice and combustor design affect heat release, soot, NOx, carbon emissions, and operability.

children.title: Nozzle expansion
children.description: Nozzles convert thermal energy and pressure into jet kinetic energy and thrust.

topics.title: Propulsion Performance, Matching, and Mission Analysis
topics.description: Shows how engine performance connects to aircraft range, endurance, climb, takeoff, and design tradeoffs.

children.title: Performance maps and matching
children.description: Students interpret component and engine maps to understand operating points and constraints.

children.title: Aircraft performance coupling
children.description: Propulsion is tied to drag, weight, climb, and range rather than analyzed in isolation.

children.title: Installed performance
children.description: Real engine performance includes nacelle, inlet, exhaust, bleed, and accessory penalties.

topics.title: Ramjets, Scramjets, and High-Speed Propulsion
topics.description: Introduces air-breathing engines for high Mach numbers, where compression, combustion, and thermal protection are governed by compressible-flow limits.

children.title: Ramjet operation
children.description: Ramjets use vehicle speed for compression and work best when dynamic pressure is high enough.

children.title: Scramjet operation
children.description: Scramjets retain supersonic flow through combustion, creating extreme mixing and heat-transfer challenges.

children.title: High-speed design constraints
children.description: Students learn why materials, cooling, inlet start, and vehicle integration dominate hypersonic propulsion.

topics.title: Rocket Propulsion Fundamentals
topics.description: Develops rocket thrust, ideal performance, and mission intuition for systems that carry both fuel and oxidizer rather than relying on atmospheric air.

children.title: Rocket thrust equation
children.description: Students learn how chamber pressure, mass flow, exhaust velocity, and pressure mismatch create rocket thrust.

children.title: Specific impulse and mass ratio
children.description: Rocket performance is framed through propellant efficiency and the exponential penalty of carrying propellant.

children.title: Nozzle expansion in rockets
children.description: Rocket nozzles are studied as devices optimized for pressure ratio, altitude, and expansion losses.

topics.title: Solid and Liquid Rocket Engines
topics.description: Compares the two major chemical rocket engine families and their tradeoffs in complexity, controllability, storage, cost, and reliability.

children.title: Solid rocket motors
children.description: Solids are simpler and storable but harder to throttle or stop once ignited.

children.title: Liquid rocket engines
children.description: Liquids enable high performance and controllability but require pumps, injectors, feed systems, and thermal management.

children.title: Engine cycles and system tradeoffs
children.description: Cycle choice shapes performance, complexity, cost, reliability, and startup behavior.

topics.title: Electric and Advanced Propulsion
topics.description: Surveys propulsion concepts that trade thrust level, efficiency, power, and mission duration differently from conventional aircraft engines and chemical rockets.

children.title: Electric spacecraft propulsion
children.description: Electric thrusters provide high specific impulse for missions where low thrust over long durations is acceptable.

children.title: Hybrid-electric aircraft propulsion
children.description: Students examine how batteries, motors, generators, and distributed propulsors change aircraft design trades.

children.title: Emerging concepts
children.description: Advanced propulsion is framed through physics limits, mission needs, technology readiness, and system integration.

topics.title: Propulsion Testing, Instrumentation, and Data Analysis
topics.description: Gives students practical awareness of how propulsion claims are measured, reduced, calibrated, and checked in labs and test facilities.

children.title: Test facility basics
children.description: Students learn what a propulsion test stand must control and measure to produce credible results.

children.title: Instrumentation and uncertainty
children.description: Measurement quality is treated as part of engineering evidence rather than an afterthought.

children.title: Data reduction
children.description: Raw measurements are converted into thrust, efficiency, fuel consumption, and performance maps.

topics.title: Environmental, Safety, and Systems Integration Considerations
topics.description: Closes the course by linking propulsion design to emissions, noise, safety, certification, operations, and whole-vehicle integration.

children.title: Environmental impacts
children.description: Students connect propulsion choices to emissions, contrails, noise, and fuel sustainability.

children.title: Safety and certification context
children.description: Propulsion systems must be designed and tested against failure modes and regulatory expectations.

children.title: Vehicle integration
children.description: Engine placement and propulsion architecture affect aerodynamics, structures, controls, thermal systems, and maintainability.
